messages:
marc_cust: Hey team — intermittent TLS handshake failures to our Redwood API over our PrivateLink endpoint since Friday. Same app works from other VPCs. vpce id vpce-0a1b2c3d. curl hangs then 'SSL handshake failed'. Any quick checks?
jordan_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a short repro (curl -v) and a couple of network checks: `dig +short <hostname>` and `traceroute -n` from the affected host? Also which OS/image and any custom DNS/forwarders?
marc_cust: Quick outputs below (redacted):
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal
192.0.2.45

$ curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health
*   Trying 192.0.2.45...
* connect to 192.0.2.45 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to api.redwood-inference.internal port 443: Connection timed out
```
We expected a private IP in 10.100.x.x for the VPCE ENI. No recent deploys on our side.
priya_neteng: Thanks — that suggests DNS resolving to a public address instead of the VPC endpoint. Two common causes: (1) private hosted zone not associated to this VPC or (2) local DNS forwarder / Route53 Resolver rules returning a public IP. Can you run: `dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2` (VPC resolver) and `dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @<your-local-dns>` and `ip route get 10.100.5.10` and `sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 port 443 -c 10`?
marc_cust: Ran those, pasted results:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @10.0.0.2
10.100.5.10

$ dig +short api.redwood-inference.internal @10.2.0.2
192.0.2.45

$ sudo tcpdump -nni eth0 port 443 -c 5
12:01:02.123456 IP 10.0.1.12.52344 > 172.31.16.1.443: SYN, seq 0, win 29200, length 0
12:01:02.123789 IP 10.0.1.12.52344 > 172.31.16.1.443: RST
```
So our instance resolver (10.2.0.2) is returning the public IP; VPC resolver returns the correct VPCE address. But TCP shows traffic going to NAT gateway (172.31.16.1) not to 10.100.5.10.
li_sre: Ok that's consistent — DNS mismatch + traffic to NAT. If your instance is using a custom DNS forwarder (10.2.0.2), it will short-circuit the VPC resolver behavior. Check your DHCP option set / EC2 instance / container DNS config. Also check if you have Route53 Resolver Outbound endpoints + conditional forward rules that send `*.internal` to an on-prem resolver.
priya_neteng: Actions to try (minimal repro steps):
1) On the instance: `sudo systemd-resolve --flush-caches` or `sudo systemctl restart systemd-resolved` (or `sudo service nscd restart`) depending on distro.
2) Re-run `dig @10.0.0.2 api.redwood-inference.internal` and `dig @127.0.0.53 api.redwood-inference.internal` to compare.
3) If custom forwarder is first in /etc/resolv.conf, either reorder so the VPC resolver (.2) is first or update your conditional forwarder rules to forward `redwood-inference.internal` to the VPC Resolver via a Route53 Resolver rule.
4) To validate connectivity without changing DNS: `curl --resolve api.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.100.5.10 https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health` — this forces the TLS SNI host while hitting the VPCE IP.
priya_neteng: Also double-check that your VPC PHZ is associated with this VPC: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-aaaa1111` and that the private zone contains `api.redwood-inference.internal`. If using a VPC resolver outbound endpoint, ensure your resolver rules are ordered so the domain is resolved locally first.
marc_cust: We found an Ops-managed DNS forwarder (10.2.0.2) that our instances used as first resolver. It would forward unknown names to our on-prem DNS which had a stale public record for `api.redwood-inference.internal`. After we reordered the DHCP option set to prefer VPC resolver and cleared the forwarder's cache, `dig` now returns `10.100.5.10`. Rechecked with curl: `curl --verbose https://api.redwood-inference.internal/health` succeeds and TLS handshake completes.
li_sre: Great — sounds like the root cause: conditional forwarder + stale cache causing a public IP return, traffic egressing via NAT, and TLS failing due to proxy/NAT path. Follow-ups:
- Ensure Route53 private hosted zone is associated and that any resolver rules for your domain point to the VPC resolver or are absent so native resolution wins.
- Add an explicit route53 rule or VPC DHCP option ordering for critical internal domains.
- If you still see intermittent failures, capture `tcpdump` during a failure to check for proxy/NAT in the path.
marc_cust: Confirmed fix: updated DHCP options, flushed caches, verified PHZ association. All green. Thanks! :tada:
jordan_support: Closing the support ticket — summary we will paste into the ticket: 1) Verify PHZ association, 2) Check instance DNS order (DHCP options), 3) Inspect Resolver rules and forwarders, 4) Use `curl --resolve` / tcpdump to validate. Reopen if it recurs.
infra-bot: Ticket #123456 closed by jordan_support — resolution: DNS forwarder returned stale public record, caused NAT egress -> TLS failures.
